proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, 7^n is congruent to 7^(n mod 10) modulo 11.

argument.text: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 50, 7^(n+10) mod 11 is congruent to 7^(n) mod 11 modulo 11.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, at least one of the following holds: n mod 4 = 0; n mod 4 = 1; n mod 4 = 2; n mod 4 = 3.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, 2*n^2 is congruent to (2*n^2) + 1001 modulo 77.
There is a integer n with 1 <= n <= 60 for which n^2 > 30.
The steps above establish the statement up to 60, and it is taken to hold for the whole range up to 60.
